earnings.title: Carrier Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results
highlights: Net sales up 12%; organic sales up 15%
GAAP EPS 2 of ($3.16); adjusted EPS 2 of $0.87
2 GAAP results include a goodwill impairment charge and IEEPA refunds; Adjusted EPS includes a ~$0.10 benefit from IEEPA refunds net of ~($0.02) NCI impact
Record >$8.5B backlog; LTA minimums additive to backlog
Net cash flows from operating activities of $813 million and free cash flow of $674 million

quotes.text: We delivered strong third quarter performance, with orders, sales and adjusted EPS all up between 15% and 35%, with very strong free cash flow.

outlook: Supported by a differentiated product portfolio, record backlog, minimum volume commitments under long-term agreements, and continued recovery in RLC end markets, Carrier now expects sales of nearly $24 billion, with organic growth of approximately 10%.

The company remains vigilant in navigating industry-wide macro pressures, including tariffs and increasing input costs, and expects to return to shareowners approximately $2.3 billion through dividends and share repurchases.

items.heading: Risks associated with our international operations could adversely affect our competitive position, results of operations, cash flows or financial condition.
We are party to joint ventures and other strategic relationships, which may not be successful and may expose us to unique risks and restrictions.
Risks associated with climate events, government regulations and incentives associated with climate events and mitigation efforts could adversely affect our business.

Our business and financial performance depend on continued and substantial investments in our information and operational technology infrastructure, which may not yield anticipated benefits and which may be vulnerable to cyber-attacks.
Cybersecurity incidents could disrupt business operations, result in the loss of critical and confidential information, and adversely impact our reputation and results of operations.

We engage in acquisitions and divestitures and may encounter difficulties integrating acquired businesses with, or disposing of businesses from, our current operations; therefore, we may not realize the anticipated benefits of these acquisitions and divestitures.
